text:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide the ordering of RBAC checks vs dashboard hydration caching for multi-tenant views. Seeing p95 spikes when tenant A runs heavy queries and we do authz post-cache lookup. thoughts?

nina: Problem statement: cached tile hits are returning data before we validate viewer perms, which requires a separate authz call and adds ~40ms on top of cache latency. p95 jumps ~20-30ms during spikes.

dario: Short answer: either bake authz into cache keys or do a pre-cache authz check. Baking into keys avoids per-request authz call but multiplies cache cardinality. Risk: if we namespace wrong we might serve data to the wrong principal.

lee: Agree with dario. My preference is namespace-by-scope: cache key includes tenantID + role-hash (not full user token) so we don't explode key space but still separate privileged vs public views. Example:
```
key := fmt.Sprintf("tiling:t=%s:scope=%s:view=%s:qh=%s", tenantID, scopeHash, viewID, queryHash)
```
This keeps shared tiles for same permission bucket.

sam: Nice. Two tradeoffs to call out: 1) more keys -> lower hit ratio and higher memory / eviction churn, 2) must ensure scopeHash updates when RBAC changes (invalidations). Nina, how often do role assignments churn?

nina: Most RBAC churn is low — org-level role changes happen a few times a day across customers, but token-level session grants rotate much more. We should avoid tying cache to ephemeral session tokens.

dario: That matches my worry. If we tie to role-hash we need an invalidation hook so that role change flushes related keys. We can emit an invalidation event from authz service. Cost of invalidation: can spike network churn.

infra-bot: perf-run queued: dashboard-hydration-prototype (shard=5) on perf-cluster-3. Test id: perf-42.

lee: Another option: two-tier cache: a shared tenant-layer with coarse-grained tiles (no user scope) and a lightweight per-session overlay for personalized fields. Shared layer keeps hit rate high; overlay is small and cheap. Eviction is easier for overlay.

sam: That feels pragmatic. Action items: (1) run perf-42 and also a variant with role-hash namespacing, (2) add an authz invalidation prototype (emit events, small consumer to evict keys), (3) prepare a short audit to ensure no data leakage if we namespace incorrectly. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up Wed.

nina: +1. I can own the invalidation audit checklist.

dario: I'll mock the two cache strategies in the staging hydra and capture hit rates.

lee: I'll draft small RFC addendum that spells out TTL recommendations and invalidation contract.

sam: Great — thanks everyone. Tagging @here for visibility. :thumbsup:
